blocks.text: An object's fields (pose, visual appearance, physics, audio) flat on the spec beside id / tags / parent / children / state / behavior / audience / lifetime / scope (the reserved words no field may take), and the same dots on the handle: crate.material.color = "red". A null write clears a field…

ObjectProperties = { feetPosition?: PositionSpec // the BOTTOM CENTRE of the shape at rest, never the geometric center; rotation turns the shape about this point (a laid log's axis passes through its feet: spell y: radius to rest it on the ground); a flat kind (plane, circle, ring, torus) and a vector picture have no feet and stand by their CENTRE, three.js's origin, so a pitch lays them flat where they are; a child: LOCAL to its parent; the world point on anything: worldFeetPosition rotation?: RotationSpec // degrees; on a child, local to the parent, read and written; the world turn: worldRotation yaw?: number // degrees; ignored when rotation is set scale?: number | Vec3 // applied after layout fits the raw model; never moves the feet attachment?: ObjectAttachmentSpec | null // with parent: bone ("RightHand") on a rigged parent; skin: true a SKINNED child model that deforms with the parent's rig; socket ("muzzle", "grip") a named point on its model; part ("turret") a piece of a ?parts= model pivot?: PivotSpec // the point of the shape that stays put when it turns: "feet" (default: the feetPosition point, the same point physics pivots on) | "center" | "top" | [u, v, w] of the bounds (v up) | { x, y, z } m: it stays where it stands at rotation 0; every rotation, the authored one too, swings the shape about it; ignored on dynamic bodies visible?: boolean // drawing only: false hides this object and everything parented under it (a child draws only while every ancestor is visible, as in three.js; a child's own word stays its own); colliders, triggers and scripts unaffected render?: boolean // drawing only; false turns off this object's OWN drawing (its primitive, model or sprite) while its collider, scripts and children stay as they are: the collider-only row, a physics hull wearing its visible body as children. `visible: false` hides the subtree; `render: false` hides the row alone visibleRange?: { min?: number; max?: number } | null // straight-line meters from the nearest view (camera, glass or live door) to its feet, not its surface; drawing only: colliders, triggers, raycasts and children unaffected; each device's draw distance scales both edges, except text, vector and ui; each edge holds a 5 % band, then fades (swaps on coarse pixels); null clears visibleInFirstPerson?: boolean | null // true keeps drawn a held item for its wielder, the player body in its own eye (hideLocalPlayer hides none of it), any rigged body the eye is in (its inside where side is "double"); the nearest explicit ancestor wins; null inherits layers?: string[] | null // the drawing layers it is on, by name (three's object.layers): a camera draws it when the camera's `layers` share a name; absent: its nearest ancestor's, else ["default"]; null inherits; [] is drawn by no camera; a light lights a view only while that view's camera draws it (the sun's and the sky's, while the screen's camera does), and a thing casts a shadow only while the screen's camera draws it; colliders, raycasts and scripts never read it visibleTo?: "all" | "editors" // "editors": players never see or meet it; children inherit at spawn only; give it physics: "none" castShadow?: boolean receiveShadow?: boolean primitive?: PrimitiveSpec spline?: SplineSpec vector?: string // The object's vector picture as SVG markup; crisp at any size and any distance, one string: `<svg viewBox="0 0 160 90" width="8m">…</svg>`. Inside: path, rect, circle, ellipse, line, polyline, polygon; <text> with font-family (serif | sans-serif | display), font-size, font-weight, font-variation-settings ('wght' 700 breathes the variable face); <g> and transform; fill/stroke/stroke-width/opacity/stroke-dasharray; linear and radial gradients from <defs>; filter="drop-shadow(0 0 blur color)" is a glow, an offset a shadow. The root's width/height are METRES (the viewBox keeps the aspect), and the viewBox's CENTRE stands at feetPosition, so half the picture hangs below it (a label on a box: the box's y + height/2); billboard="none" (default: the object's own rotation) | "yaw" | "full". In a 2D place, the root's sortingLayer and sortingOrder sort the picture as a sprite of that layer and order with ySort off. Set them to seat it among the sprites. Several elements in one string are one object with one collider (its box). A write is the picture on the next frame; a tween of the string: animate(ctx, id, { vector: NEXT }, { duration }): cross-fades paired shapes for its seconds. A tag or attribute outside the subset is a named fault on the row and the rest paints. model?: | string | { id: string; offset?: [number, number, number]; forward?: ForwardAxis; animation?: { clip?: string; speed?: number; loop?: "once" | "loop" | "pingpong" }; materials?: Record<string, Omit<StandardMaterialSpec, "time" | "timeAt" | "paused" | "speed"> | ScriptedMaterialSpec>; parts?: Record<string, ModelPartStateSpec> } // the .glb the object wears; a wisp's Blender export or a creator's upload (`/cdn/value.<sha>.glb`); the clips its file carries play by name on a mixer channel and every other clip by address (`mixer.<channel>.clip`); a creature that walks from code is a code rig instead: skeleton() beside geometry(), its clips your data; offset (`[x, y, z]` or `{ x, y?, z }` metres) moves the mesh only, the physics stays put; forward: for a model that stands turned round, the axis it was built to face: `forward: "+z"` turns it half round onto the engine's −Z once, sockets and parts with it (omitted: no turn; a model the platform made already faces −Z, and "+z" on it turns nothing) mixer?: Record< string, { clip: string; weight?: number; duration?: number; speed?: number; loop?: "once" | "loop" | "pingpong"; blendIn?: number; blendOut?: number; direction?: "normal" | "reverse" | "alternate"; mask?: { from: string } | { bones: string[] }; blend?: "normal" | "override" | "additive"; time?: number; timeAt?: number; talking?: true; clampWhenFinished?: true } > | null // animation channels: `{ clip, weight, loop, speed, blend }`; channels share each bone property by weight (`blend: "normal"`, the default: two at weight 1 are half each), and `blend: "override"` lifts the channel above that shared blend so it replaces what its clip touches, whole, by its own weight (a face over a body clip, an aim over a walk); `blend: "additive"` adds its clip's motion since its first frame on top of both, by its weight (a reload over an idle); at runtime write ctx.self.anim.<ch> = { clip, weight, loop } | "clip" | weight | null jiggle?: boolean | JiggleSpecValue | JiggleSpecValue[] | null // spring bones: ears, a tail, hair or a skirt swing and settle on a model's or a skeleton()'s bones, no script; true: joints named like hair, ears, a tail or a skirt spring; amount 0..1 is how much of the body's own movement (its travel and turning) the chains feel: 0 rides along (animation, gravity and colliders still move them), 1 feels all of it; `wind: { force }` bends them in the place's wind; `radius` (metres, the joints' thickness) + `colliders` (spheres/capsules on named bones, this model's or another entity's, the chains never pass through: hair rests on the shoulders); a LIST of such rows gives each chain set its own knobs (`[{ bones: ["Hair_F*"], amount: 0 }, { bones: ["Pony*"], amount: 0.6 }]`); visual only; null removes morph?: MorphSpecValue | null // Shape-key (morph target / blend shape) weights on the model: target name → weight, e.g. `{ Blink: 1 }` or `{ Smile: 0.6, JawOpen: 0.3 }`. Names are the GLB's (Blender shape-key names): `getObjectMorphTargetNames(id)` lists them; a numeric string like "0" addresses a target by index. Targets you name override the playing clip's `weights` track for that target; targets you don't name keep the clip's. Weights are unclamped (1.5 over-drives, -0.5 inverts). `null` hands the whole face back to the clip. Purely presentational. bones?: BonesSpecValue | null // The pose, as state; bone name → `{ pitch, yaw, roll }` in degrees about the bone's own local x / y / z (in that order; a positive pitch tips the bone's own −Z up, as three.js's rotation.x). Each rig sets its bones' axes: a bone's line is the localPosition of the `<entity>.skeleton` row whose parentName is that bone, a turn about that line twists the limb in place, and a turn about either other axis swings it. `{ x, y, z }` is metres along its parent's axes. Both add over whatever clips play: `self.bones.jaw.pitch = -28` drops a jaw hinged at the back (its −Z tip falls) and every screen sees the thing's own write next frame; `animate(ctx, id, { "bones.jaw.pitch": 0 }, { duration: 0.2 })` closes it; a breath, a lean, a wag are curves written here every few ticks. Names are the rig's bones: a scripted geometry's `skeleton()` export, or the GLB's joints (`<entity>.skeleton` lists them); a name the rig lacks does nothing. `{ rotate: [x, y, z], offset: [x, y, z] }` is the same turn and move as triples. `null` hands the rig back to the clips. Applied on each screen after the mixer and before IK. The pose is presentational. To pose another player's body per screen, write its bones from a script on an `audience: "local"` thing, reading shared state; each screen leans that body itself, and only the state is sent. `self.bones.<bone>.reach`: Put a bone at a point: its two parents bend (a hand on a handle, a foot on a rock), and a point past their length leaves the limb straight toward it. The target is a world point { x, y, z } or { object, offset? }, followed every frame: a point written each tick moves smoothly between ticks. A `rotation` on the target sets the bone's turn as `currentWorldRotation` reads it, in the object's frame on an object target. A humanoid's hand turns only as far as a human wrist bends: with no `pole` the elbow swings to reach the turn, and a `pole` keeps the elbow where it puts it as far as a human shoulder turns, past that the elbow swings to where the shoulder and the hand's turn both hold. Long form { to, pole?, weight?, blendIn?, blendOut? }: `pole` is the point the middle joint bends toward (an elbow out, a knee forward); null lets go. `self.bones.<bone>.aim`: Turn a bone so that its front (-Z) points at a point: a head looks, an eye stalk follows, a turret tracks. Same targets as reach, without rotation or pole. `self.bones.<bone>.ground`: 0 to 1: keep a bone on the ground under it. A foot rests on a slope, and the body sinks so that its lowest foot reaches. A foot its clip holds still stays planted while the body moves, and steps to keep up. A grounded ankle stands at its height in the model's rest pose. Any number of feet. A humanoid model's feet have it already (1, read on the blended pose, not per channel), as `LeftFoot` and `RightFoot` whatever its file calls them: 0 on a foot draws it as its clip holds it (a fall, a kneel); null gives it back. `self.bones.<bone>.scale`: Multiply a bone's size as the clips play it, and every bone under it follows (1 = as played): 0 shrinks a limb's skin to its joint (an arm cut off, a head gone), 2 doubles it. `self.bones.<bone>.visibleInFirstPerson`: false hides the bone and every bone under it from its own player's eye while the body draws from inside that eye (`hideLocalPlayer = false`, the eye in the head), as the engine hides the head there: legs and torso in first person under view-model arms. Other players, mirrors and the shadow keep it. Default true. `self.bones.<bone>.mass`: The kilograms the bone weighs when the body ragdolls (`self.ragdoll`), read as it goes limp: `self.bones.Spine.mass = 25` makes a heavy torso that falls first. Every bone without one keeps its share of the body's mass (`physics.mass`, split by each part's thickness), and the body weighs the sum. sprite?: { // a flat image facing the camera: billboard yaw (unset) turns the card to each viewer's camera, none locks it to the entity's rotation (a flat thing: a decal, a poster: edge-on from the side), full also pitches; uvRect picks a sheet region; frames named in events fire onAnimationEvent; castShadow: true throws the card's shadow in its picture's shape (a turning card's shadow turns with it) texture: AssetID size?: [number, number] // World-space [width, height] of the quad. OMIT for pixel sprites: the engine sizes the sprite from the asset's declared world height (its `2d` metadata), so pixel density stays uniform across the scene (64 px per world unit). Set it only to deliberately rescale; authored size always beats the metadata default. pixelsPerUnit?: number // Pixels-per-unit convenience; used only when `size` is omitted. Setting it also opts out of the metadata-driven default size. anchor?: [number, number] // Normalized [u, v] point of the art that sits at the entity's origin (0..1, v up; default [0.5, 0] = bottom-center "feet"). It places the quad relative to `feetPosition`, it is the pivot the sprite rotates around: a bullet spinning about its center wants [0.5, 0.5], a ceiling lantern swinging from its top wants [0.5, 1], a door hinged at an edge wants [0, 0], and the auto-derived collider2d hull is expressed against the same point, so art, pivot, and hitbox always share one origin. tint?: Color // multiplies the art opacity?: number // 0..1, blends in linear light: over a dark background white at 0.05 reads 21% solid, 0.25 reads 65%, 0.5 reads 86% blend?: SpriteBlendMode lit?: boolean // Scene lights shade the sprite (the engine derives a normal map from the art automatically). Default: in a 2D place that has any authored light, world sprites are lit automatically: painted plates (`backdrop-`, `strip-`, `floor-` art and parallax layers) stay unlit because their lighting is in the art, and an explicit true/false always wins. Places without lights render unlit. Alpha/cutout blends only: add/multiply/subtract sprites are themselves light/stain, so `lit` is a documented no-op there. emissive?: number // HDR glow (default 0). Feeds bloom; works lit or unlit. normalStrength?: number // Normal-map relief strength (default 1). 0 = pure distance falloff. billboard?: "none" | "yaw" | "full" upright?: boolean // The sprite never inherits the entity's rotation as in-plane spin; it keeps the base pose (axis-aligned under the camera) however the entity turns: NPC steering, physics, scripts. The lock covers both 2D modes. The collider of a body that is not dynamic stays with the picture too; rotation still drives children and a dynamic body. Characters whose facing is `?facing=` texture swaps want `upright: true`; leave unset for things that should visibly turn (cars, ships, banking projectiles). No effect in 3D places: `billboard` owns rotation inheritance there. flipX?: boolean flipY?: boolean sortingLayer?: number sortingOrder?: number ySort?: boolean alphaCutoff?: number cutout?: boolean // Alpha-tested cutout rendering: discard pixels below 50% alpha and write depth, so heavily overlapping sprites (foliage, crowds, dense beds) resolve per-pixel instead of haloing by draw order. Default on for pixel-inferred art (`pixel-*` names, `?animated=` atlases, `scripts/tex-*.js` refs), off for painterly art, which sorts whole-sprite by distance: set true on a painterly sprite that lives among others, false for soft/glow edges. filter?: "pixel" | "linear" // Texture sampling override. "pixel" samples nearest (crisp pixel art), "linear" samples smooth. Unset defers to the asset's own pixel-ness (moodboard grammar / metadata inference). parallax?: [number, number] // Scroll factors [x, y] of a background picture; the sim never moves it. 1 = fixed in the world (default), 0 = fixed to the camera, between = parallax (far hills ~0.2–0.5, near trees ~0.7). It draws at feet + (1 − factor) × camera: the first factor on x, the second on z in a 2d-top place and on y elsewhere. A `backdrop-` picture in a 2D place whose second factor is not 1 also stays on screen on that axis. repeatX?: boolean // Tile the sprite's texture along X. On camera-attached sprites the quad spans the viewport and the texture scrolls its UV phase (the strip recipe). On plain world sprites this only sets the sampler's wrap: the sprite keeps its own class (lit stays lit, batched stays batched); use `uvRect` width > 1 for the tile count, or pair with `feetPosition: { attach: "camera" }` for an endless band. uvRect?: SpriteUvRect // Normalized texture-space rectangle; UV origin is bottom-left. Inside 0..1 it crops (a still cell of a sheet). Reaching past 0..1 tiles: the sampler wraps on that axis: `{ x: 0, y: 0, width: 4, height: 1 }` repeats the art 4× across the quad, with no lighting or batching side effects. A negative width or height reads the crop mirrored (the sprite-engine mirror); zero is refused. events?: Record<string, Record<number, string>> | null // Frame events, per clip: `events: { run: { 3: 'footfall', 7: 'footfall' } }`: the clip name a mixer channel plays, the frame index (clip-local) that fires the named event exactly when the winning channel's clock shows that frame. The object's behavior receives it as `onAnimationEvent(ctx, { name, animation, frame })`: footsteps, attack hitboxes, emitter bursts that never drift from the art. Set null to remove. Costs nothing on sprites without it. trail?: { interval?: number; life?: number; count?: number; tint?: Color | [Color, Color]; fade?: "alpha" | "shrink" | "both"; blend?: "normal" | "additive" } | null // Afterimage trail, dash ghosts, motion echoes: `trail: { interval: 0.04, life: 0.3, fade: 'both' }`. The engine snapshots the sprite's pose + frame + tint every `interval` seconds and draws the snapshots behind the sprite, fading out over `life` seconds (`fade`: 'alpha' | 'shrink' | 'both'; `tint` recolors the ghosts; `count` caps them). `tint` also takes a `[head, tail]` ramp of two colours lerped per ghost by age. `blend: 'additive'` renders the ghosts add-blended for energy/glow dashes (the sprite itself keeps its own blend). Ghosts are frozen copies: they never animate. Set null to remove. Costs nothing on sprites without it. material?: ScriptedMaterialSpec // A scripted material draws the sprite's pixels: `{ kind: "scripted", script, params }`, the contract an object's material takes; what it reads of the sprite is ctx.sprite (spawn api builtin/three). The sprite keeps its size, frames, flips, tint, opacity, blend, cutout and sorting; the material's class decides its light, so lit, emissive and normalStrength do nothing. Each distinct params value is its own batch and its own draw. A broken script draws the plain sprite until the next edit. } wisp?: WispSpec | null // a living pixel-wisp burning from its row (voxels in 3D, the pixel grid in 2D); null removes it boxart?: BoxartSpec | null // a game's printed box, cracked open by a player's press into a portal to the game; null removes it collider2d?: { outline: [number, number][] } // Manual 2D collider override. Outline is normalized [0,1] in IMAGE space (x right, y DOWN: the same convention as MCDN hull metadata); ≥3 usable points become a convex polygon collider hugging the sprite art, degenerate outlines fall back to a tight bounding box. When absent, the engine hydrates the hull from the texture's MCDN metadata automatically: authored collider2d always beats the hydrated hull. In a 2D place v = 1 is the sprite's FEET: a tall top-down sprite a walker should bump at its trunk takes a foot band (`[[0.32, 0.86], [0.68, 0.86], [0.68, 1], [0.32, 1]]`); a band higher in the image sits up-screen of the trunk and the walker passes under it. ui?: string | null // A panel painted on this object: your HTML, as ui.js writes it (Tailwind and all), laid out and drawn onto the object's face: culled, lit and occluded with the object, riding its pose with no lag. 1 CSS px = 1 mm. Attributes on the root element place it: face="front|back|left|right|top|bottom" (front is its −Z, the way it faces; top reads upright from the front), at="u v" (0..1 across the face), width="0.32m", offset="0.005m", facing="player" (turns upright toward each viewer: a sign) or facing="screen" (square to the screen, as a sprite: a nameplate, a health bar), emissive (a screen: the panel bypasses the light). Braces read this object's own row live: {{ state.score | pad 6 }} in text, disabled="{{ state.running }}" on an attribute (a boolean keeps or drops it); filters pad N · fixed N · round · upper · lower · default X; the engine re-derives the panel when the state it reads changes, so write state, never repaint. A press on <button id="start"> rings ctx.on("ui:start", (ctx, { by }) => …); an id-less element rings "ui" with { by, tag }. Rewrite the string to change the layout; null clears it. room?: RoomSpec // auto floor + walls around this object: compat; an interior is scripted geometry (geometry skill) layout?: LayoutSpec // fits the raw model into min/max extents before scale; ignored on children material?: MaterialSpec light?: LightSpec audio?: AudioIntentValue // a clip on this object, also a song a game seeks, pauses or draws a bar for (`time`, `paused`, `spatial: false`): the room's on an `audience: "all"` object, one player's with `listeners`; ctx.music.* has no seek or pause (audio skill). `.level`: this machine's loudness of this sound now, 0..1 (0 where not heard; never shared between players); metered only while a script reads it. `.readout`: what its program voice's readout() returns on this machine, undefined until it answers voice?: { gain: number } | null // on a player: how loud the people around hear their voice, gain 0..1 (0 silent for them); null = 1; on anything that is not a player it does nothing. A team voice room keeps its own post (social skill) fx?: FxSpec // an effect script scripts/effects/<name>.fx.js (fx skill) interpolation?: { teleportThreshold: number } | null // null turns off smoothing between ticks physics?: ObjectPhysics // omitted = NO collider (walk-through): anything walked on or into needs one; "character" for what walks; collider "mesh" rides a static or kinematic body, never a dynamic one. Reads back as the object form on every copy: `{ body, collider?, … }`, a string shorthand spelled into it; null where no body is authored. air?: boolean // true: its inside is air. The place's sea and ground water stay out of its convex hull, so a body in it stands dry and an eye in it sees no underwater tint, fog or distortion: a glass dome, a diving bell, a submarine's cabin. A hollow that is not convex is several such things. With `visible: false` it is an air volume of its own shape. A pool or a tank inside it is its own water. press?: PressContactSpec | PressContactSpec[] | null // what leans the ground cover (the blades lean away and spring back in ~1 s): omitted = the body's own contacts: a walker its feet ({ radius: 0.6, strength: 1 }), a dynamic body its whole footprint, a wheeled appliance its hull's footprint and each wheel, a seated walker nothing: the ride presses; { radius, strength? } at the feet, or a list [{ at: [x, y, z], radius, strength?, below? }]: a car hull's four wheel contacts; [] presses nothing; null = the body's own again scatter?: ScatterSpec // a bed of instances over an area (heightmap-terrain skill) blueprint?: { label?: string; category?: string; icon?: string } // a god-mode palette entry }

  spline?: SplineSpec

  model?: | string | { id: string; offset?: [number, number, number]; forward?: ForwardAxis; animation?: { clip?: string; speed?: number; loop?: "once" | "loop" | "pingpong" }; materials?: Record<string, Omit<StandardMaterialSpec, "time" | "timeAt" | "paused" | "speed"> | ScriptedMaterialSpec>; parts?: Record<string, ModelPartStateSpec> }   // the .glb the object wears; a wisp's Blender export or a creator's upload (`/cdn/value.<sha>.glb`); the clips its file carries play by name on a mixer channel and every other clip by address (`mixer.<channel>.clip`); a creature that walks from code is a code rig instead: skeleton() beside geometry(), its clips your data; offset (`[x, y, z]` or `{ x, y?, z }` metres) moves the mesh only, the physics stays put; forward: for a model that stands turned round, the axis it was built to face: `forward: "+z"` turns it half round onto the engine's −Z once, sockets and parts with it (omitted: no turn; a model the platform made already faces −Z, and "+z" on it turns nothing)
  mixer?: Record< string, { clip: string; weight?: number; duration?: number; speed?: number; loop?: "once" | "loop" | "pingpong"; blendIn?: number; blendOut?: number; direction?: "normal" | "reverse" | "alternate"; mask?: { from: string } | { bones: string[] }; blend?: "normal" | "override" | "additive"; time?: number; timeAt?: number; talking?: true; clampWhenFinished?: true } > | null   // animation channels: `{ clip, weight, loop, speed, blend }`; channels share each bone property by weight (`blend: "normal"`, the default: two at weight 1 are half each), and `blend: "override"` lifts the channel above that shared blend so it replaces what its clip touches, whole, by its own weight (a face over a body clip, an aim over a walk); `blend: "additive"` adds its clip's motion since its first frame on top of both, by its weight (a reload over an idle); at runtime write ctx.self.anim.<ch> = { clip, weight, loop } | "clip" | weight | null
  jiggle?: boolean | JiggleSpecValue | JiggleSpecValue[] | null   // spring bones: ears, a tail, hair or a skirt swing and settle on a model's or a skeleton()'s bones, no script; true: joints named like hair, ears, a tail or a skirt spring; amount 0..1 is how much of the body's own movement (its travel and turning) the chains feel: 0 rides along (animation, gravity and colliders still move them), 1 feels all of it; `wind: { force }` bends them in the place's wind; `radius` (metres, the joints' thickness) + `colliders` (spheres/capsules on named bones, this model's or another entity's, the chains never pass through: hair rests on the shoulders); a LIST of such rows gives each chain set its own knobs (`[{ bones: ["Hair_F*"], amount: 0 }, { bones: ["Pony*"], amount: 0.6 }]`); visual only; null removes
  morph?: MorphSpecValue | null   // Shape-key (morph target / blend shape) weights on the model: target name → weight, e.g. `{ Blink: 1 }` or `{ Smile: 0.6, JawOpen: 0.3 }`. Names are the GLB's (Blender shape-key names): `getObjectMorphTargetNames(id)` lists them; a numeric string like "0" addresses a target by index. Targets you name override the playing clip's `weights` track for that target; targets you don't name keep the clip's. Weights are unclamped (1.5 over-drives, -0.5 inverts). `null` hands the whole face back to the clip. Purely presentational.
  bones?: BonesSpecValue | null   // The pose, as state; bone name → `{ pitch, yaw, roll }` in degrees about the bone's own local x / y / z (in that order; a positive pitch tips the bone's own −Z up, as three.js's rotation.x). Each rig sets its bones' axes: a bone's line is the localPosition of the `<entity>.skeleton` row whose parentName is that bone, a turn about that line twists the limb in place, and a turn about either other axis swings it. `{ x, y, z }` is metres along its parent's axes. Both add over whatever clips play: `self.bones.jaw.pitch = -28` drops a jaw hinged at the back (its −Z tip falls) and every screen sees the thing's own write next frame; `animate(ctx, id, { "bones.jaw.pitch": 0 }, { duration: 0.2 })` closes it; a breath, a lean, a wag are curves written here every few ticks. Names are the rig's bones: a scripted geometry's `skeleton()` export, or the GLB's joints (`<entity>.skeleton` lists them); a name the rig lacks does nothing. `{ rotate: [x, y, z], offset: [x, y, z] }` is the same turn and move as triples. `null` hands the rig back to the clips. Applied on each screen after the mixer and before IK. The pose is presentational. To pose another player's body per screen, write its bones from a script on an `audience: "local"` thing, reading shared state; each screen leans that body itself, and only the state is sent. `self.bones.<bone>.reach`: Put a bone at a point: its two parents bend (a hand on a handle, a foot on a rock), and a point past their length leaves the limb straight toward it. The target is a world point { x, y, z } or { object, offset? }, followed every frame: a point written each tick moves smoothly between ticks. A `rotation` on the target sets the bone's turn as `currentWorldRotation` reads it, in the object's frame on an object target. A humanoid's hand turns only as far as a human wrist bends: with no `pole` the elbow swings to reach the turn, and a `pole` keeps the elbow where it puts it as far as a human shoulder turns, past that the elbow swings to where the shoulder and the hand's turn both hold. Long form { to, pole?, weight?, blendIn?, blendOut? }: `pole` is the point the middle joint bends toward (an elbow out, a knee forward); null lets go. `self.bones.<bone>.aim`: Turn a bone so that its front (-Z) points at a point: a head looks, an eye stalk follows, a turret tracks. Same targets as reach, without rotation or pole. `self.bones.<bone>.ground`: 0 to 1: keep a bone on the ground under it. A foot rests on a slope, and the body sinks so that its lowest foot reaches. A foot its clip holds still stays planted while the body moves, and steps to keep up. A grounded ankle stands at its height in the model's rest pose. Any number of feet. A humanoid model's feet have it already (1, read on the blended pose, not per channel), as `LeftFoot` and `RightFoot` whatever its file calls them: 0 on a foot draws it as its clip holds it (a fall, a kneel); null gives it back. `self.bones.<bone>.scale`: Multiply a bone's size as the clips play it, and every bone under it follows (1 = as played): 0 shrinks a limb's skin to its joint (an arm cut off, a head gone), 2 doubles it. `self.bones.<bone>.visibleInFirstPerson`: false hides the bone and every bone under it from its own player's eye while the body draws from inside that eye (`hideLocalPlayer = false`, the eye in the head), as the engine hides the head there: legs and torso in first person under view-model arms. Other players, mirrors and the shadow keep it. Default true. `self.bones.<bone>.mass`: The kilograms the bone weighs when the body ragdolls (`self.ragdoll`), read as it goes limp: `self.bones.Spine.mass = 25` makes a heavy torso that falls first. Every bone without one keeps its share of the body's mass (`physics.mass`, split by each part's thickness), and the body weighs the sum.
  sprite?: {   // a flat image facing the camera: billboard yaw (unset) turns the card to each viewer's camera, none locks it to the entity's rotation (a flat thing: a decal, a poster: edge-on from the side), full also pitches; uvRect picks a sheet region; frames named in events fire onAnimationEvent; castShadow: true throws the card's shadow in its picture's shape (a turning card's shadow turns with it)
    texture: AssetID
    size?: [number, number]   // World-space [width, height] of the quad. OMIT for pixel sprites: the engine sizes the sprite from the asset's declared world height (its `2d` metadata), so pixel density stays uniform across the scene (64 px per world unit). Set it only to deliberately rescale; authored size always beats the metadata default.
    pixelsPerUnit?: number   // Pixels-per-unit convenience; used only when `size` is omitted. Setting it also opts out of the metadata-driven default size.
    anchor?: [number, number]   // Normalized [u, v] point of the art that sits at the entity's origin (0..1, v up; default [0.5, 0] = bottom-center "feet"). It places the quad relative to `feetPosition`, it is the pivot the sprite rotates around: a bullet spinning about its center wants [0.5, 0.5], a ceiling lantern swinging from its top wants [0.5, 1], a door hinged at an edge wants [0, 0], and the auto-derived collider2d hull is expressed against the same point, so art, pivot, and hitbox always share one origin.
    tint?: Color   // multiplies the art
    opacity?: number   // 0..1, blends in linear light: over a dark background white at 0.05 reads 21% solid, 0.25 reads 65%, 0.5 reads 86%
    blend?: SpriteBlendMode
    lit?: boolean   // Scene lights shade the sprite (the engine derives a normal map from the art automatically). Default: in a 2D place that has any authored light, world sprites are lit automatically: painted plates (`backdrop-`, `strip-`, `floor-` art and parallax layers) stay unlit because their lighting is in the art, and an explicit true/false always wins. Places without lights render unlit. Alpha/cutout blends only: add/multiply/subtract sprites are themselves light/stain, so `lit` is a documented no-op there.
    emissive?: number   // HDR glow (default 0). Feeds bloom; works lit or unlit.
    normalStrength?: number   // Normal-map relief strength (default 1). 0 = pure distance falloff.
    billboard?: "none" | "yaw" | "full"
    upright?: boolean   // The sprite never inherits the entity's rotation as in-plane spin; it keeps the base pose (axis-aligned under the camera) however the entity turns: NPC steering, physics, scripts. The lock covers both 2D modes. The collider of a body that is not dynamic stays with the picture too; rotation still drives children and a dynamic body. Characters whose facing is `?facing=` texture swaps want `upright: true`; leave unset for things that should visibly turn (cars, ships, banking projectiles). No effect in 3D places: `billboard` owns rotation inheritance there.
    flipX?: boolean
    flipY?: boolean
    sortingLayer?: number
    sortingOrder?: number
    ySort?: boolean
    alphaCutoff?: number
    cutout?: boolean   // Alpha-tested cutout rendering: discard pixels below 50% alpha and write depth, so heavily overlapping sprites (foliage, crowds, dense beds) resolve per-pixel instead of haloing by draw order. Default on for pixel-inferred art (`pixel-*` names, `?animated=` atlases, `scripts/tex-*.js` refs), off for painterly art, which sorts whole-sprite by distance: set true on a painterly sprite that lives among others, false for soft/glow edges.
    filter?: "pixel" | "linear"   // Texture sampling override. "pixel" samples nearest (crisp pixel art), "linear" samples smooth. Unset defers to the asset's own pixel-ness (moodboard grammar / metadata inference).
    parallax?: [number, number]   // Scroll factors [x, y] of a background picture; the sim never moves it. 1 = fixed in the world (default), 0 = fixed to the camera, between = parallax (far hills ~0.2–0.5, near trees ~0.7). It draws at feet + (1 − factor) × camera: the first factor on x, the second on z in a 2d-top place and on y elsewhere. A `backdrop-` picture in a 2D place whose second factor is not 1 also stays on screen on that axis.
    repeatX?: boolean   // Tile the sprite's texture along X. On camera-attached sprites the quad spans the viewport and the texture scrolls its UV phase (the strip recipe). On plain world sprites this only sets the sampler's wrap: the sprite keeps its own class (lit stays lit, batched stays batched); use `uvRect` width > 1 for the tile count, or pair with `feetPosition: { attach: "camera" }` for an endless band.
    uvRect?: SpriteUvRect   // Normalized texture-space rectangle; UV origin is bottom-left. Inside 0..1 it crops (a still cell of a sheet). Reaching past 0..1 tiles: the sampler wraps on that axis: `{ x: 0, y: 0, width: 4, height: 1 }` repeats the art 4× across the quad, with no lighting or batching side effects. A negative width or height reads the crop mirrored (the sprite-engine mirror); zero is refused.
    events?: Record<string, Record<number, string>> | null   // Frame events, per clip: `events: { run: { 3: 'footfall', 7: 'footfall' } }`: the clip name a mixer channel plays, the frame index (clip-local) that fires the named event exactly when the winning channel's clock shows that frame. The object's behavior receives it as `onAnimationEvent(ctx, { name, animation, frame })`: footsteps, attack hitboxes, emitter bursts that never drift from the art. Set null to remove. Costs nothing on sprites without it.
    trail?: { interval?: number; life?: number; count?: number; tint?: Color | [Color, Color]; fade?: "alpha" | "shrink" | "both"; blend?: "normal" | "additive" } | null   // Afterimage trail, dash ghosts, motion echoes: `trail: { interval: 0.04, life: 0.3, fade: 'both' }`. The engine snapshots the sprite's pose + frame + tint every `interval` seconds and draws the snapshots behind the sprite, fading out over `life` seconds (`fade`: 'alpha' | 'shrink' | 'both'; `tint` recolors the ghosts; `count` caps them). `tint` also takes a `[head, tail]` ramp of two colours lerped per ghost by age. `blend: 'additive'` renders the ghosts add-blended for energy/glow dashes (the sprite itself keeps its own blend). Ghosts are frozen copies: they never animate. Set null to remove. Costs nothing on sprites without it.
    material?: ScriptedMaterialSpec   // A scripted material draws the sprite's pixels: `{ kind: "scripted", script, params }`, the contract an object's material takes; what it reads of the sprite is ctx.sprite (spawn api builtin/three). The sprite keeps its size, frames, flips, tint, opacity, blend, cutout and sorting; the material's class decides its light, so lit, emissive and normalStrength do nothing. Each distinct params value is its own batch and its own draw. A broken script draws the plain sprite until the next edit.
  }
  wisp?: WispSpec | null   // a living pixel-wisp burning from its row (voxels in 3D, the pixel grid in 2D); null removes it
  boxart?: BoxartSpec | null   // a game's printed box, cracked open by a player's press into a portal to the game; null removes it
  collider2d?: { outline: [number, number][] }   // Manual 2D collider override. Outline is normalized [0,1] in IMAGE space (x right, y DOWN: the same convention as MCDN hull metadata); ≥3 usable points become a convex polygon collider hugging the sprite art, degenerate outlines fall back to a tight bounding box. When absent, the engine hydrates the hull from the texture's MCDN metadata automatically: authored collider2d always beats the hydrated hull. In a 2D place v = 1 is the sprite's FEET: a tall top-down sprite a walker should bump at its trunk takes a foot band (`[[0.32, 0.86], [0.68, 0.86], [0.68, 1], [0.32, 1]]`); a band higher in the image sits up-screen of the trunk and the walker passes under it.
  ui?: string | null   // A panel painted on this object: your HTML, as ui.js writes it (Tailwind and all), laid out and drawn onto the object's face: culled, lit and occluded with the object, riding its pose with no lag. 1 CSS px = 1 mm. Attributes on the root element place it: face="front|back|left|right|top|bottom" (front is its −Z, the way it faces; top reads upright from the front), at="u v" (0..1 across the face), width="0.32m", offset="0.005m", facing="player" (turns upright toward each viewer: a sign) or facing="screen" (square to the screen, as a sprite: a nameplate, a health bar), emissive (a screen: the panel bypasses the light). Braces read this object's own row live: {{ state.score | pad 6 }} in text, disabled="{{ state.running }}" on an attribute (a boolean keeps or drops it); filters pad N · fixed N · round · upper · lower · default X; the engine re-derives the panel when the state it reads changes, so write state, never repaint. A press on <button id="start"> rings ctx.on("ui:start", (ctx, { by }) => …); an id-less element rings "ui" with { by, tag }. Rewrite the string to change the layout; null clears it.
  room?: RoomSpec   // auto floor + walls around this object: compat; an interior is scripted geometry (geometry skill)
  layout?: LayoutSpec   // fits the raw model into min/max extents before scale; ignored on children
  material?: MaterialSpec
  light?: LightSpec
  audio?: AudioIntentValue   // a clip on this object, also a song a game seeks, pauses or draws a bar for (`time`, `paused`, `spatial: false`): the room's on an `audience: "all"` object, one player's with `listeners`; ctx.music.* has no seek or pause (audio skill). `.level`: this machine's loudness of this sound now, 0..1 (0 where not heard; never shared between players); metered only while a script reads it. `.readout`: what its program voice's readout() returns on this machine, undefined until it answers
  voice?: { gain: number } | null   // on a player: how loud the people around hear their voice, gain 0..1 (0 silent for them); null = 1; on anything that is not a player it does nothing. A team voice room keeps its own post (social skill)
  fx?: FxSpec   // an effect script scripts/effects/<name>.fx.js (fx skill)
  interpolation?: { teleportThreshold: number } | null   // null turns off smoothing between ticks
  physics?: ObjectPhysics   // omitted = NO collider (walk-through): anything walked on or into needs one; "character" for what walks; collider "mesh" rides a static or kinematic body, never a dynamic one. Reads back as the object form on every copy: `{ body, collider?, … }`, a string shorthand spelled into it; null where no body is authored.
  air?: boolean   // true: its inside is air. The place's sea and ground water stay out of its convex hull, so a body in it stands dry and an eye in it sees no underwater tint, fog or distortion: a glass dome, a diving bell, a submarine's cabin. A hollow that is not convex is several such things. With `visible: false` it is an air volume of its own shape. A pool or a tank inside it is its own water.
  press?: PressContactSpec | PressContactSpec[] | null   // what leans the ground cover (the blades lean away and spring back in ~1 s): omitted = the body's own contacts: a walker its feet ({ radius: 0.6, strength: 1 }), a dynamic body its whole footprint, a wheeled appliance its hull's footprint and each wheel, a seated walker nothing: the ride presses; { radius, strength? } at the feet, or a list [{ at: [x, y, z], radius, strength?, below? }]: a car hull's four wheel contacts; [] presses nothing; null = the body's own again
  scatter?: ScatterSpec   // a bed of instances over an area (heightmap-terrain skill)
  blueprint?: { label?: string; category?: string; icon?: string }   // a god-mode palette entry
}
